_comment: Recovery levers as data, not branches: an operator can add or retune one
by editing this file, without a code change.
The four families are NOT equivalent, and that distinction is the point:
QUEUE      changes WHO misses, never how many. Free and instant.
THROUGHPUT reduces misses. Costs money, and arrives after a lead time.
INFLOW     reduces misses among FUTURE arrivals only. Costs revenue.
PROMISE    reduces breaches without touching the work. Costs goodwill.
Every number here is a demo default, not business truth.

levers.name: Protect a customer segment
levers.description: Pin one cohort to the front of the queue. Zero-sum: everyone behind them moves back by exactly as much.
side_effects: Orders outside the segment are pushed later

levers.name: Defer the orders with most slack
levers.description: Push orders with more than half a day of room behind those running out of it. Changes the order of misses, not the number.
side_effects: Deferred orders lose slack they may later need

levers.name: Extend the shift
levers.description: Hold staff past the end of shift to add picking capacity. Real extra throughput, at overtime rates, and only once people actually stay.

levers.name: Suspend value-added services
levers.description: Pause gift wrap, personalisation and inserts for the surge window. Removes work from every order rather than adding capacity.
side_effects: Customers who paid for gift wrap do not receive it

levers.name: Book a late carrier pickup
levers.description: Move the collection later so work already finishing today still ships today. Buys dispatch time without buying capacity, and is consistently the cheapest real win available.
side_effects: Carrier may charge for an out-of-schedule collection

levers.name: Pause the promotion
levers.description: Stop pouring water in while bailing. Affects orders not yet placed, so it rescues nobody already queued.

levers.name: Hide express at checkout
levers.description: Remove the tightest promise from the storefront for the surge window. Stops new express commitments the floor cannot keep.

levers.name: Extend the promised date
levers.description: Re-promise pending orders with proactive notification. Changes the commitment rather than the work.
side_effects: Every affected customer must be told

levers.name: Apologise with credit
levers.description: For orders already beyond rescue, convert a silent breach into a managed one. This is not a save: the order is still late, the customer just hears it from us first.
side_effects: Does not make any order arrive sooner

postures.title: Do Nothing
postures.trades: Nothing. This is what happens if no one acts.

postures.title: Catch the Late Pickup
postures.trades: A collection fee, against orders that miss today's van by minutes.

postures.title: Buy the Hour
postures.trades: Money for throughput: overtime plus dropping value-added work.

postures.title: Protect New Customers
postures.trades: First-order buyers are saved; repeat buyers absorb the delay.

postures.title: Defer the Comfortable
postures.trades: Orders with slack to spare wait, so tighter ones move up. Nobody is rescued; the misses move.

postures.title: Close the Tap
postures.trades: Revenue now, to stop the backlog growing further.

postures.title: Manage the Miss
postures.trades: Goodwill and credits, for breaches that cannot be prevented.
